producer_report.summary: Added the records-history cutover. `[history] cutover_job` is optional in config.rs and set to this job's id in athena.toml. When `athena land --pr` lands that job, a new `LandingRecords::cutover` hook runs after the landing record. It reads `cutover_job` from the landed commit's athena.toml, takes C0 from the landing record's host commit, and appends one commit to the remote records tip. That commit holds `records/` at C0, `import-manifest.json` (checked by `verify_cutover_import`), and `legacy-exempt.json`. The exempt record is built from `[history] exempt` at C0 (seven entries, each with a reason). The same routine runs as a catch-up at the end of `Athena::try_reconcile`, the step `land` and `status` run first. Each file is written only if it is missing, so a second run writes nothing. A failure in the land path is a warning, and in reconcile a line, never an error. `check_history` now routes: with no `cutover_job`, no records branch, no landing, or a landing without a manifest naming C0, it is exactly the old check (the manifest-less case adds a visible "pending" note). Once the manifest names C0, commits up to C0 are judged by the old rules with the exempt list from the legacy-exempt record, and later commits only by attribution (findings reported as `Rule::JobRecords`). Gitleaks still runs over every commit. ci.yml keeps the job name "the full history" and fetches `athena/records` before the check, with the checkout token kept (`contents: read`) and the fetch skipped on pull requests. D119 in decisions.md and a CHANGELOG entry record the design. Trailers are untouched. Full suite, clippy with warnings denied, and fmt check all pass.

criteria_check.evidence: gh::tests::records_flow::cutover_land_imports_at_c0_and_writes_the_legacy_exempt_record (run with `cargo test -p athena-core cutover_land`). It drives the free `land_pr` with a bare remote and a fake host, using a world where the PR commit's athena.toml names the job and the checkout's base has none. It asserts the landing record, one import commit on top of it, `verify_cutover_import` passing, the manifest naming C0, and a legacy-exempt record with 7 entries (one is 02837e0), each with a non-empty reason. C0 comes from `cutover_commit_at(...) == landing.host_commit`. Passed in the full suite.

A second reconcile leaves the tip and count unchanged. A sibling test shows that with the import already present only legacy-exempt.json is added.

open_issues: Departures from the plan, for the user to accept or redirect. (1) The land path resolves `cutover_job` inside `GitLandingRecords::cutover` from the host commit, so there is no `with_cutover` builder and `Athena::land_pr` is unchanged. (2) Besides reconcile.rs, which the plan flagged, `manage.rs` (a `notes` field on `CheckReport`) and `athena-cli/src/main.rs` (print the notes) were also touched, to show the pending note. None of these is in the brief's file list.

The CI history job skips the records fetch on pull requests, so a PR head is judged by the old rules. With the fetch on PRs, every post-C0 PR would fail attribution because its commits cannot be named by a landing before they merge. This reads 'fetches athena/records first' as true for pushes, the schedule and manual runs. A person running `athena check --history` on a branch with a local athena/records is judged by records.

Whether the athena binary that lands this very job predates this change is not knowable from the code. If it does, the import runs only when a newer binary runs `athena status` or `athena land`. Until then CI stays on the old rules (cutover pending), by design.
The cutover hook skips quietly when the host commit cannot be fetched. The reconcile catch-up then finishes the work.
After C0 the content, invariant and prediction checks no longer run on main's commits. Only attribution and gitleaks do. This is as requested, and D119 notes it.
The routing and the real-repository behavior were tested on scratch repositories only; nothing was run against the real remote.
mistakes: First draft of the 'no cutover job' reconcile test asserted the records tip was unchanged, but reconcile itself repairs a missing landing record. I corrected it to assert the catch-up wrote nothing.
First draft of the catch-up test counted commits with `rev-list --count` including the landing's second parent. Fixed with --first-parent.
learnings: `athena_gate::BUILTIN_CONFIG` is `include_str!` of the repo's athena.toml, so the built-in config now names this job as the cutover job. `cutover_job_for` therefore reads the commit's own athena.toml and ignores the built-in config.
`RecordsWriter::append_to_remote` pushes with an expected-tip guard, so the import, manifest and legacy-exempt record go in one commit, and a second import onto a branch with a manifest is refused.
`git rev-list --count` on the records branch counts a landing's extra parent (the PR head), so tests count with --first-parent.

The existing `legacy.rs` already had `check_attribution_with_legacy`, `legacy_exempt_record` and `legacy_exempt_change`, so the gate needed only routing and a cutover-state reader. Only `attribution.rs` (listed) and `history.rs` changed in the gate, apart from `legacy.rs` tests, which were not touched.
`Athena::reconcile` needs `origin/HEAD` set locally (`git remote set-head origin main`) to find the default branch without a host client; the reconcile tests do this.
desires: A way to build a throwaway `Athena` for tests without repeating the fake driver and pinner setup in each module.
A way to run the real `athena land --pr` against a scratch GitHub repository, to see the cutover end to end.
